subject: ACME - MAP: Technical Eval Plan (draft)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>, Kevin Lee <kevin.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: ACME - MAP: Technical Eval Plan (draft)

Hi Sarah / Kevin —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. Per our call I put together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan focused on the Technical Evaluation milestone so we can align on success criteria and responsibilities before your SRE/ML infra team kicks off the benchmark. Attached: ACME_MAP_v1.pdf and a simple benchmark_template.xlsx that Michael and I will use for the tests.

Key items in this draft (high level):
- Milestone: Technical Evaluation (owner: ACME / co-owner: Redwood SE)
  - Success criteria: baseline accuracy/quality pass rate on the 200-case prompt set, latency p95 target, and cost-per-1k-token budget.
  - Latency target (p95): <= 350 ms for 512-token context (internal target, open to adjustment based on infra)
  - Cost target: goal <$1.50 / 1k tokens (token accounting in template)
  - Model shortlist: Llama-2-13b-chat, Mistral-7B-v1.0, Falcon-40B-Instruct, redwood/v2-7b (quantized) — we will benchmark equivalent-sized variants where possible.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (latency, cost, quality), reproducible runbook, and a recommendation for model variant + config.
- Dependencies: access to a staging endpoint or sample traffic, dataset/seed prompts from ACME, and SRE time for infra verification (network egress, VPC peering, or Dedicated test reservation).
- Target close for this milestone: 2027-04-23 (aiming to complete benchmarking and recommendation).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the model shortlist and latency/cost targets by EOD Wed (2027-04-07) — please flag if your SRE or procurement needs adjustments.
2) ACME to share the core 200-case prompt set and a small representative production sample (anonymized) by Thu (2027-04-08).
3) Redwood SE (Michael) will schedule a 60-min runbook/infra sync with your SREs — proposed windows in the attached doc.

If you prefer a different target close date, tell us and we'll update the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v1.pdf, benchmark_template.xlsx

From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Lee <kevin.lee@acme.com>, acme-security@acme.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: ACME - MAP: Technical Eval Plan (draft)

Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap and for drafting the MAP. A few quick clarifications from our side before we confirm: 

- Latency target: the 350 ms p95 is reasonable as a starting point, but our internal SREs prefer that we run a pair of baseline tests at both 350 ms and a relaxed 500 ms to understand cost tradeoffs. Can Michael include both thresholds in the benchmark template?
- Cost: the <$1.50 / 1k tokens target is useful as a ballpark. Our procurement team will want to see the cost broken down by token type (prompt vs. completion) and by model variant.
- Model shortlist: would you be able to include a quantized 4-bit variant where available? We want to understand throughput gains vs quality trade-offs.

We will share the anonymized prompt set by Thu (2027-04-08). Kevin — can you loop in SRE availability for the week of Apr 12?

Thanks,
Sarah

--
Sarah Johnson
Director, Product AI — ACME Corp
sarah.johnson@acme.com

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - MAP: Technical Eval Plan (draft)

Hi Sarah / Camila —

Thanks — I took the MAP and updated the benchmark_template.xlsx to include dual-latency thresholds (p95 @ 350 ms and p95 @ 500 ms) and separate columns for prompt vs completion token accounting. Also added a column for quantized 4-bit runs where supported. I'll attach the updated template to the runbook we share during the infra sync.

Proposed benchmark success criteria (suggested, happy to adjust):
- Functional quality: >= 85% pass rate on the 200-case prompt set (binary pass/fail per prompt based on your rubric)
- Latency: p95 <= 350 ms (primary) and p95 <= 500 ms (cost baseline) for 512-token context
- Cost: median cost <= $1.50 / 1k tokens for the primary model; report comparative costs across variants
- Stability: no more than 1% inference error rate (exceptions/timeouts) during a sustained 1-hour run at 50 RPS equivalent traffic

Model/variant shortlist for the technical run (we'll try to match size and quantization across vendors):
- meta/llama-2-13b-chat (float32 / int8 / 4-bit quant)
- mistral/mistral-7b-v1.0 (float32 / 4-bit quant)
- together/falcon-40b-instruct (float32 / int8 where possible)
- redwood/v2-7b (optimized kernels, int8/4-bit variants)

Run logistics:
- ACME to provide prompt set + representative traffic by 2027-04-08
- Redwood to provision Dedicated test reservation on Apr 12-14 (need SRE ok for VPC peering or a short-lived public staging endpoint)
- Michael to run small-scale warm-up runs Apr 12-13, full comparative runs Apr 14-15
- Deliverable: benchmark report and recommended model/config by Apr 23

If that timeline looks good, I'll send calendar invites for the infra sync and the run windows.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: benchmark_template_v2.xlsx (to be uploaded to Drive)

Thanks for the MAP and benchmark approach. SRE are available the week of Apr 12 for a 60-min infra/runbook sync — I scheduled: Tue Apr 13 10:00-11:00 EDT (invite sent). We'll bring a rep from procurement to the runbook so they can see token accounting and cost breakdowns live.

Kevin
